system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

[FCC-HI-2018#0084] Report and Recommendations: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency January 13, 2018 False Alert (p.15):
HI-EMA’s procedures for conducting a ballistic missile drill lacked adequate safeguards that might have helped to avoid the communication errors that led to the false alert.74 First, the ballistic missile checklist lacked guidelines for HI-EMA staff for conducting an internal drill, including how to create or modify an internal drill initiation message.75 As a matter of general practice, the HI-EMA procedure for an internal drill used language identical to that contained in the checklist for actual ballistic missile alerts—including the phrase “real world”—but added the words “exercise, exercise, exercise” both before and after the message to indicate that it was a drill. Use of the same language for both test and live alert initiation procedures could cause confusion among warning officers who received the message without prior notice, notwithstanding the statements at the beginning and end of the message that it was an exercise.

data.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin on hazard, wind, visibility, places and end time. One fault: the description ends with "This is not a drill.", which contradicts the Exercise status and the EXERCISE labelling. This is a hazard-fact and certainty problem the drafter can fix. The start time (10:30) is omitted, which is minor and not blocking.

objections.issue: The description says "This is not a drill." while status is Exercise and the headline and description are marked EXERCISE. This contradicts the bulletin context and could lead recipients to treat an exercise as a real event, as in the Hawaii false alert, where mixed exercise and "not a drill" wording caused confusion.
objections.fix: Delete "This is not a drill." and keep the exercise labelling consistent, e.g. end with "This is an exercise."

evidence.quote: a second message includes “This is not a drill.”

no_basis.concern: The alert gives only the end time (until 18:00) and omits the start at 10:30. The bulletin says conditions began at 10:30, so the alert does not contradict it.
no_basis.searched_for: CAP onset or effective time requirements for NCM dust warnings

no_basis.concern: Severity "Moderate" and the "Observed" certainty look consistent with the bulletin, which describes ongoing conditions. No clause sets a severity level for dust events in the UAE.
no_basis.searched_for: CAP 1.2 severity urgency certainty definitions Observed Immediate
